epa_echo_sdwa.name: EPA ECHO — Safe Drinking Water Act, community water systems
epa_echo_sdwa.note: Active community water systems, the municipalities they serve and two of ECHO's compliance flags. The observatory publishes counts for each municipality, never a system's name.

epa_echo_cwa.name: EPA ECHO — Clean Water Act, wastewater discharge permits (NPDES)
epa_echo_cwa.note: Facilities with an active individual permit to discharge wastewater, with ECHO's current compliance status. The observatory publishes counts for each municipality, never a facility's name or point.

epa_echo_caa.name: EPA ECHO — Clean Air Act, stationary sources of air pollution
epa_echo_caa.note: Active facilities that the Clean Air Act regulates, with EPA's class of their emissions. The observatory publishes counts for each municipality, never a facility's name or point.

epa_echo_rcra.name: EPA ECHO — Hazardous waste handlers (RCRA)
epa_echo_rcra.note: Active handlers of hazardous waste, with their class by the amount they generate. The observatory publishes counts for each municipality, never a handler's name or point.

epa_echo_all.name: EPA ECHO — Inspections and enforcement actions at regulated facilities
epa_echo_all.note: Active facilities regulated under the air, water, hazardous waste or drinking water laws, with their inspections and formal enforcement actions of the last five years. The observatory publishes counts for each municipality, never a facility's name or point.

epa_tri.name: EPA — Toxics Release Inventory (TRI), Basic Data File for Puerto Rico
epa_tri.license: EPA Standard Open Data License: public domain (17 U.S.C. 105)
epa_tri.note: Pounds of listed toxic chemicals that the reporting facilities released in the reporting year. The observatory sums them for each municipality; it publishes no name, address or point.

eia_860m.name: EIA — Form EIA-860M, Monthly Update to the Annual Electric Generator Report
eia_860m.note: Operating generators of Puerto Rico. The observatory publishes plants and capacity for each municipality, never owner or plant names.

vars.label: Community water systems serving the municipality
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Safe Drinking Water Act: active community water systems
vars.definition: Active community water systems (systems that serve the same people all year: PRASA's, the community-run systems known as non-PRASA, and one federal system) that list the municipality among those they serve. A system that serves several municipalities counts in each, so the municipal values add up to more than Puerto Rico's, which counts each system once (and also the few small systems that give no municipality).

vars.label: Water systems with a health-based violation
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Safe Drinking Water Act: active community water systems
vars.definition: Of those systems, the ones ECHO flags with a health-based violation: a breach of a maximum contaminant level, a maximum residual disinfectant level or a treatment technique rule. It is a compliance record, not proof that the water is unsafe today.

vars.label: Water systems that are an enforcement priority
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Safe Drinking Water Act: active community water systems
vars.definition: Of those systems, the ones EPA designates as an enforcement priority: unresolved serious, multiple or continuing violations.

vars.label: Community water systems outside PRASA (non-PRASA)
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Safe Drinking Water Act: active community water systems
vars.definition: Of those systems, the ones the Safe Drinking Water Information System (SDWIS) records as privately owned: the community-run systems known as non-PRASA, which EPA Region 2 defines as the privately owned systems, and a few private developments and institutions. SDWIS records some community-run systems as local government, so this count can miss a few. A system that serves several municipalities counts in each; Puerto Rico's value counts each system once. Names are never published: many systems are named after a person, a family or a farm.

vars.label: Residents served by community water systems outside PRASA
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Safe Drinking Water Act: active community water systems
vars.definition: The population that the non-PRASA systems (privately owned in SDWIS) report serving, added up for the systems that serve only this municipality. A system that serves several municipalities is left out of every municipality's value, because its population cannot be split, and is counted in Puerto Rico's value. The population served is the system's own estimate.

vars.label: Facilities with a permit to discharge wastewater
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Clean Water Act: facilities with an active individual NPDES permit
vars.definition: Facilities with an active individual permit to discharge wastewater into rivers, lakes or the sea (a permit of the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System, NPDES, which EPA issues in Puerto Rico): sewage treatment plants, water filtration plants, power plants, factories and others, in the municipality that holds the facility's point. Not counted: the facilities covered by a general permit (construction sites and stormwater), which come and go with each project.

vars.label: Public sewage treatment plants
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Clean Water Act: facilities with an active individual NPDES permit
vars.definition: Of those facilities, the publicly owned treatment works (POTW): the plants that treat the sewage of homes and businesses before it is discharged. In Puerto Rico the Aqueduct and Sewer Authority (PRASA) runs nearly all of them. A plant counts in the municipality where it stands, which may not be the only one it serves.

vars.label: Major wastewater dischargers
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Clean Water Act: facilities with an active individual NPDES permit
vars.definition: Of those facilities, the ones EPA classes as major: sewage treatment plants built to treat 1 million gallons a day or more, and industrial facilities that EPA scores as major for the volume or the pollutants of their discharge.

vars.label: Wastewater dischargers with a violation on record
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Clean Water Act: facilities with an active individual NPDES permit
vars.definition: Of those facilities, the ones whose current status in ECHO is 'Violation Identified' or 'Significant/Category I Noncompliance': a discharge above a permit limit, a missed deadline of a compliance schedule, or a monitoring report that was late or never sent. It is a compliance record of the last reported quarter, not a measure of how clean the water is today, and a late report counts the same as a discharge above a limit.

vars.label: Facilities regulated for air pollution
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Clean Air Act: active stationary sources of air pollution
vars.definition: Active stationary sources of air pollution that the Clean Air Act regulates and EPA's ECHO lists: power plants, factories, quarries and asphalt plants, fuel terminals, hospitals and others with boilers, generators or processes that emit into the air, in the municipality that holds the facility's point. Most are minor sources. Cars, trucks and other moving sources are not facilities and are not counted.

vars.label: Major sources of air pollution
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, Clean Air Act: active stationary sources of air pollution
vars.definition: Of those facilities, the ones EPA classes as major emissions sources: they emit, or could emit, more than the Clean Air Act's thresholds (in most areas 100 tons a year of a regulated pollutant, or 10 tons a year of one hazardous air pollutant), and need a Title V operating permit. Major is a class of size, not a finding that the facility breaks its permit.

vars.label: Hazardous waste handlers
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, RCRA: active handlers of hazardous waste
vars.definition: Active handlers of hazardous waste that EPA's ECHO lists under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA): the businesses and institutions that generate hazardous waste (factories, laboratories, hospitals, auto shops, dry cleaners and others), and those that transport, treat or store it, in the municipality that holds the handler's point. Most generate very small amounts.

vars.label: Large generators of hazardous waste
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, RCRA: active handlers of hazardous waste
vars.definition: Of those handlers, the large quantity generators: they generate 1,000 kilograms or more of hazardous waste in a month (or more than 1 kilogram of acutely hazardous waste), and must follow the strictest rules for storing, shipping and reporting it. Large is a class of amount, not a finding that the handler breaks the rules.

vars.label: Facilities inspected for environmental compliance
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, all programs: active regulated facilities, last five years
vars.definition: Of the active facilities that EPA regulates under the air, water, hazardous waste or drinking water laws, the ones that EPA or the Puerto Rico government inspected at least once in the last five years, in the municipality that holds the facility's point. An inspection is a routine check, not a finding that something is wrong.

vars.label: Facilities with a formal environmental enforcement action
vars.ref: EPA ECHO, all programs: active regulated facilities, last five years
vars.definition: Of those facilities, the ones that received at least one formal enforcement action in the last five years: an order or a court case in which EPA or the Puerto Rico government requires the facility to correct a violation, with or without a penalty. A warning letter or notice of violation is an informal action and is not counted.

vars.label: Toxic chemicals released, pounds
vars.ref: EPA Toxics Release Inventory, reporting year 2024
vars.definition: The pounds of listed toxic chemicals that the facilities reporting to EPA's Toxics Release Inventory released in 2024, on site (to the air, to water, to land) and off site (sent elsewhere for disposal), summed for the municipality that holds each facility's point. Only larger facilities in certain industries report, and only for the chemicals on EPA's list. Pounds of different chemicals are added together, so the figure shows amount, not toxicity or risk.

vars.label: Toxic chemicals released to the air, pounds
vars.ref: EPA Toxics Release Inventory, reporting year 2024
vars.definition: Of those pounds, the ones released on site to the air in 2024, from stacks and vents and as leaks and evaporation (fugitive emissions). Pounds of different chemicals are added together, so the figure shows amount, not toxicity or risk.

vars.label: Power plants (operating)
vars.ref: EIA-860M, operating generators
vars.definition: Plants with at least one operating generator in EIA's monthly inventory, in the municipality that holds the plant's point. Plants whose generators add up to less than 1 MW, most rooftop solar among them, are not in the inventory.

vars.label: Generating capacity, MW (nameplate)
vars.ref: EIA-860M, operating generators
vars.definition: The nameplate capacity of the operating generators in the municipality, in megawatts: how much the generators are built to produce, not what they produce. Batteries are left out (they store power).

vars.label: Renewable generating capacity, MW (solar, wind, hydro, landfill gas)
vars.ref: EIA-860M, operating generators
vars.definition: The nameplate capacity of the operating solar, wind, hydroelectric and landfill gas generators in the municipality, in megawatts. Rooftop solar is not in EIA's inventory.

water.note: A system that serves several municipalities counts in each; its population is not split.

wastewater.note: Only individual permits are counted. A facility is placed by its point; its name and point are not kept.

air.note: A source is placed by its point; its name and point are not kept. The sources with a violation are too few to publish for each municipality: the count is given for Puerto Rico only.

hazwaste.note: A handler is placed by its point; its name and point are not kept. The handlers with a violation are too few to publish for each municipality: the count is given for Puerto Rico only.

enforcement.note: A facility is placed by its point; its name and point are not kept. A drinking water system is placed at the point ECHO gives it, often its office.

tri.note: Pounds are summed by municipality; no name or point is kept. In a municipality with one reporting facility the figure is that facility's own public report.
